headline: Nvidia to fulfill only 1% of China's $70B AI GPU order amid supply constraints
summary: Chinese tech giants expected to receive only tens of thousands of RTX Pro 5500 GPUs, despite massive demand and a $70 billion order.
details: Nvidia is reportedly only able to fulfill approximately 1% of the massive $70 billion order for RTX Pro 5500 workstation GPUs placed by Chinese technology giants like ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent. Sources suggest that only "some tens of thousands" of these AI-focused chips will be delivered in the coming months.

The demand for the RTX Pro 5500 has significantly outpaced Nvidia's production capabilities. Earlier reports indicated orders for over 3 million GPUs, with the total value now estimated at $70 billion, at a cost of $11,000 per unit. This demand is driven by China's race to develop advanced AI models.

The RTX Pro 5500 is a powerful GPU for AI tasks, featuring the same CUDA cores as the flagship gaming GPU, the RTX 4090, and an impressive 84GB of GDDR7 memory. Crucially, it does not face the same export restrictions as other high-end AI chips, making it a key component for China's AI ambitions.

Chinese developers anticipate the first batch of several thousand RTX Pro 5500 GPUs by the end of 2026. Nvidia is expected to deliver around 700,000 units by the end of 2027 as production scales up, though these figures remain subject to change.

Nvidia has declined to comment on specific shipment numbers but has criticized existing U.S. export controls, which it claims hinder its ability to supply products, alongside China's own import limitations.
